title: FREI DAY FOR FUTURE - Shaping healthy and sustainable living environments together
summary: The study examines the contribution of schools to healthy and sustainable lifestyles and living conditions. The focus is on whether the introduction of the FREI DAY learning format promotes this in a special way and what burdens or reliefs this entails for schools. Ninety schools are participating in the study, some of which have decided to implement FREI DAY and some of which have not (yet) done so. Participation in the study is straightforward and involves only a very manageable amount of effort. All participating schools receive annual summary reports on their results, which can be used as a basis for funding applications and for data-driven school development. In addition, schools are offered free webinars on how to use the results in school practice and to initiate targeted changes. At least one school class (min. 20 students) and 5-12 key persons (e.g., school staff, parent representatives) are surveyed per school and school year. At FREI DAY schools, all individuals actively involved in the development, implementation, and design of FREI DAY (FREI DAY team) are also surveyed. Some FREI DAY schools are also subject to qualitative research. The study uses quasi-experimental methods to calculate the causal effects of FREI DAY from the data. In addition, the study includes a practical transfer strategy. This ensures that the findings of the study are promptly put into practice by politicians and schools, thus making a practical difference.
conditions: Health promotion and education for sustainable development
